name: 09-bash-notes-cli
shape_of: A longer-form build than 08-cli-centipede. The agent has to design and implement a multi-subcommand bash CLI plus its own end-to-end test suite, then iterate when the tests catch bugs. Expected trajectory: write the script, write the tests, run them, fix what fails, repeat. Pushes turn count past one-shot territory.
prompt:
Build a bash CLI called `notes` (script `./notes` at workspace root, executable) that manages plain-text notes. Required subcommands and behaviors:

- `./notes help` -- print usage including every subcommand below.
- `./notes add "<title>"` -- read content from stdin until EOF, create a new note with that title and content. Print the new note's numeric id (e.g. `3`) to stdout, nothing else.
- `./notes list` -- print one note per line in the form `<id>\t<title>` (tab-separated), sorted by id ascending. No header.
- `./notes show <id>` -- print the note's BODY (not title, not id) to stdout. Exit 1 with a message on stderr if the id doesn't exist.
- `./notes rm <id>` -- delete the note. Exit 0 on success, exit 1 on missing id.
- `./notes search "<query>"` -- print the ids (one per line, ascending) of notes whose title OR body contains the query, case-insensitive.

Storage:
- Notes live under `$NOTES_DIR` (must default to `$HOME/.notes` if unset). Create the directory if it doesn't exist.
- IDs are positive integers, monotonically increasing from 1, never reused.
- Format / on-disk layout is your choice -- just keep it consistent. Suggest one file per note.

Also write `tests/test_notes.sh` -- an executable bash script that:
- Sets `NOTES_DIR` to a fresh temp dir.
- Exercises every subcommand end-to-end (add 2 notes, list, search, show, rm, list again).
- Prints `PASS` and exits 0 if everything works; prints a `FAIL: <what>` line and exits 1 otherwise.
- Cleans up the temp dir on exit.

When `./tests/test_notes.sh` exits 0, run the oracle's scripted scenario yourself to sanity-check, then say done. Iterate on test failures if any come up. Don't say done until your own tests pass.
